s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 60s
The subcutaneous node was first noticed 10 years ago
The node has been slowly growing
The patient experienced swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
The swelling disappeared with lactation
The patient experienced mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
The tumor cells are positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
The tumor cells are negative for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
One of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells

differentials: dermal analogue of mammary Paget disease
per_call: dermal analogue of mammary Paget disease

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for apocrine markers and estrogen receptor, consistent with apocrine gland origin

shortlist.label: Apocrine carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Tumor cells are positive for GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies, indicating apocrine differentiation

shortlist.label: Extramammary Paget disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of cytokeratin 20 and GATA3 positivity, which can be seen in extramammary Paget disease

shortlist.label: Secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological features, including the presence of a dermal tumor with a diffuse infiltration pattern

shortlist.label: Mammary-type eccrine carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Tumor cells are positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, and estrogen receptor, which can be seen in mammary-type eccrine carcinoma

raw.rationale: The tumor's location in the axilla, its slow growth, and the presence of apocrine glands in close association with the tumor cells, along with the immunohistochemical profile (positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3), are consistent with hidradenocarcinoma, a rare malignant tumor originating from apocrine or eccrine glands.

rejected.label: Apocrine carcinoma
rejected.why: While the tumor is associated with apocrine glands, the term apocrine carcinoma is more commonly used in the context of breast cancer, and the clinical presentation and histopathology here are more suggestive of a primary skin adnexal tumor.

rejected.label: Extramammary Paget disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a different clinical and histological picture, often involving the epidermis and having a distinct immunohistochemical profile that includes positivity for cytokeratin 7 and HER2, which is not mentioned here.

rejected.label: Secretory carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that can occur in the breast or salivary glands, and while it shares some immunohistochemical features, the clinical context and specific markers do not align perfectly with the case description.

rejected.label: Mammary-type eccrine carcinoma
rejected.why: The description provided does not specifically align with the characteristics of mammary-type eccrine carcinoma, which might show different histological and immunohistochemical features, and the term is less commonly used in this context compared to hidradenocarcinoma.
